question: Do the Action Plan and the MPRs address all potential pollution contributors on the Shimsha stretch?
intro: The Shimsha's CPCB polluted stretch runs Yediyur to Halagur bridge (Priority IV). This section compares the KSPCB Action Plan's commitments with what the monthly progress reports actually report. 'Not reported' means absent from the documents, not necessarily absent on the ground.

primary.label: NMCG Monthly Progress Report (Karnataka, Shimsha stretch)
primary.note: August 2025 is the last stretch-wise MPR edition; April 2026 annexures provide the latest STP and water-quality status.

actionPlan.label: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Shimsha

baseline.banner: The August 2025 MPR is the last stretch-wise edition we hold; from October 2025 the format drops per-stretch narrative, and by April 2026 the MPR carries only state-wide annexure tables (station classes, STP lists). Accountability below anchors on the August 2025 stretch-wise reporting, with April 2026's annexures as the latest outcome data.
otherSources: NMCG MPR April 2026 - annexure tables only (station water-quality classes + state-wide STP lists); no per-stretch narrative

regions.name: Maddur (TMC)
regions.inBasinNote: The stretch ULB - population 28,902, on the Bengaluru-Mysuru corridor.

categories.label: Public STPs

actionPlan.summary: 100% UGD for the town, a terminal STP to CPCB standards, no untreated discharge, treated sewage to irrigation (actions 1-3); a 3.5 MLD low-cost facility already existed in 2019.

mpr.summary: The good-news story now carries an asterisk in the MPR's own hand. August 2025: the Rs 50.15 crore upgrade to 6 MLD is 'completed and under operation', network and household-connection works 70% done - but the same section records that the TMC has NOT obtained consent for establishment-expansion and has NOT applied for renewal of consent under the Water Act: the upgraded plant runs unconsented. April 2026's annexures then contradict the utilisation claim: the 6 MLD plant is listed operational at 1.5 MLD utilisation (against August's claimed 3.5/3.5), while the same plant also appears in the under-construction annexure at ~25% progress with completion re-set to 26.12.2026.

gaps: The completion timeline printed in the stretch reports is still 14-04-2022; the April 2026 annexure quietly re-sets it to 26.12.2026 - a 4.7-year slip visible only by reading two annexures against each other.
August's 3.5 MLD 'fully utilised' vs April's 1.5 MLD utilisation is a 2.3x discrepancy between two editions of the same report series, with no explanation offered.
Operating an upgraded STP without CFE-expansion or consent renewal is a violation recorded by the MPR itself, with no enforcement action reported.

categories.label: Solid Waste

actionPlan.summary: MSW including poultry and slaughter-house waste to be disposed only at MSW sites, never on the river banks (action 4); the plan records ~9 TPD generation and bank dumping.

mpr.summary: August 2025: 10 TPD generated; 70% of wet waste home-composted, 30% at a decentralised plant; Rs 5.25 crore integrated SWM DPR (work order 23-03-2020) with civil work 70% complete; sanitary landfill still under construction (gap 2.4 TPD). The Huthgere landfill authorisation that expired on 31.12.2021 remains expired - the line is unchanged across editions, with no renewal reported.

gaps: The landfill authorisation lapse is reported but carries no renewal status.
Slaughter-house and poultry waste - specifically named in the plan - has no dedicated reporting line.

actionPlan.summary: Biomedical waste does not appear in the Shimsha Action Plan.
actionPlan.cite: Shimsha Action Plan (full text, zero mentions)

mpr.summary: 81.7 kg/day across 3 bedded and 26 non-bedded facilities; disposed to CBMWTF (M/s Maridi Eco Solutions). Unchanged through the August 2025 edition.

categories.label: Fecal Sludge

actionPlan.summary: Faecal sludge and septage do not appear in the Action Plan.

mpr.summary: Movement at last, in the April 2026 annexures: two Maddur FSTPs are in procurement - 0.25 MLD MBBR (agreement concluded 27.06.2025, survey under way) and 0.20 MLD MBBR (DPR approved in SLTC, technical bids under evaluation). Neither appears in any stretch-wise edition; the action plan never committed faecal-sludge treatment.

gaps: Until the network closes, the unconnected households' septage is the unaccounted flow.

mpr.summary: No private STP reporting for Maddur in any edition.

regions.name: Industry on the stretch
regions.inBasinNote: The plan tables industrial units within 5 km of the river; the MPR reports one water-polluting industry on the stretch.

categories.label: Industrial effluent

actionPlan.summary: Category-wise inventory of units within 5 km of the river, with treatment status per unit.

mpr.summary: One water-polluting industry reported, generating 2.9 MLD of effluent with its own ETP - a single source producing nearly as much effluent as the entire town's sewage (3.5 MLD).

gaps: One factory ~ one town in effluent terms, yet its compliance is a single line with no published effluent data or continuous monitoring.

regions.name: Gram Panchayats (Shimsha stretch)
regions.inBasinNote: The rural tank-cascade country between Yediyur and Halagur.
regions.silentNote: No MPR edition and no Action Plan item reports anything at gram-panchayat level for this stretch - in the basin's largest tank country (222 MI tanks), the rural reach is unreported in the official accountability trail.
